reference.title: Barbell Incline Reverse Grip Press
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the bar lowers, hold briefly at the chest, breathe out as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a light touch, about 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen and lighter than your incline bench press; the underhand grip is harder to control. Leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep touches the chest with the elbows tucked.

cues.text: Back pad at about 30 degrees, shoulder blades back and down, feet planted. Underhand grip a little wider than the shoulders, thumbs wrapped around the bar; take the bar out to straight arms over the shoulders.
Lower the bar to the lower chest with the elbows close to the body and the forearms vertical.
Touch lightly, no bounce; wrists stacked over the elbows.
Press up and slightly back to straight arms over the shoulders; breathe out.
Steady the bar at the top before the next rep.

mistakes.fix: Wrap the thumbs around the bar; the underhand bar can roll out of open hands.
Keep the bar low in the palm over the forearm bones.
Keep the elbows tucked; that is the point of the reverse grip.

mistakes.mistake: Bar touching too high on the chest
mistakes.fix: Bring it to the lower chest so the forearms stay vertical.

kinematics.norm: About 30 degrees raises upper-chest and front-deltoid work over a flat bench (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020; Lauver 2016)
Underhand, about shoulder width or a little wider (common coaching)
About 90 degrees or more with the bar on the chest (clinical opinion)
Elbows close to the trunk, about 15-30 degrees (common coaching)
From the lower chest to over the shoulders (common coaching)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Incline Reverse Grip Press, video (movement reference only)

Rodríguez-Ridao, Antequera-Vique, Martín-Fuentes and Muyor 2020, effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339; PMC7579505)
Lauver, Cayot and Scheuermann, influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise (Eur J Sport Sci, 2016; PubMed 25799093)

cautions: Press inside a rack with safeties or with a spotter; never press heavy alone without safeties.
Use a spotter for the hand-off: unracking an underhand bar is awkward.
Wrap the thumbs around the bar.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort: lighter bar, or a neutral-grip dumbbell incline press instead.
Shoulder pain: lower bench angle, shorter range.
regressions: Barbell incline close grip bench press.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pressing muscle; the incline and the underhand grip shift work toward the upper (clavicular) fibres (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020; Lauver 2016).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pressing muscle; the incline and the underhand grip shift work toward the upper (clavicular) fibres (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020; Lauver 2016).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Works hard on an incline, more so as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Works hard on an incline, more so as the bench rises (Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straighten the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straighten the elbows to lock out.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Assist at the shoulder with the forearms supinated and help control the descent.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Assist at the shoulder with the forearms supinated and help control the descent.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blades against the ribs as the bar goes up.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Keeps the shoulder blades against the ribs as the bar goes up.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blades back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the shoulder blades back and down on the bench.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the bar in the underhand grip; the wrists want to bend back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the bar in the underhand grip; the wrists want to bend back.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the back in a slight natural arch.

phases.label: Arms straight, bar over the shoulders

guides.label: Press back up over the shoulders
